answer: An agent earns a ballot only by holding exclusive title to one charted harbor range lantern, with its flash period and color sectors enrolled against two unaffiliated shore cameras and a pile-mounted current meter. Mid-epoch a registrar names a minute on the incoming tide; both cameras must record the same flash phase, and the meter has to track the berth's predicted current. Keys that share a single lantern, or fake a lamp indoors, produce a bearing wander the cameras flag, and the bond is slashed. One real lantern supports one vote.
